name: Xt4b – AI Blog Posts
author: lbcw

sections.description:
This plugin is the opt-in alternative to Xt4b’s hosted blog. Instead of serving
posts from a blog hostname, it reads them from Xt4b’s read API (/api/v2/posts)
and creates ordinary WordPress posts, so your editorial process can stay in
wp-admin.

New to Xt4b? It is the service this plugin imports from: you connect your domain,
Xt4b finds the searches you are missing, writes a post for each one, and publishes
them to a blog on your own domain. Read about it, and create an account, at
https://xt4b.com. The trial is seven days and needs no card. The plugin does
nothing until you paste an API key, so start there if you are only browsing.

An Xt4b account is required, and Xt4b is a paid service: 20€ per website, per
language, per month, after the seven day trial. The plugin itself has no paid
tier and no locked features. All of it is GPLv2 and does the same work whether the
account is on a trial or a subscription; what the service returns is what it
imports. Service terms: https://xt4b.com/terms-of-service.

  • Pull, never push. WordPress does not need to be reachable from the internet;
    the API key is a read-only credential scoped to your Xt4b account.
  • Idempotent. Every import is matched to its local post by _xt4b_post_id,
    and a content fingerprint means an unchanged post is never rewritten.
  • Safe by default. New posts arrive as drafts, in the default category, with
    no publishing until you release them.
  • Reconciles unpublishes. If a post is no longer published in Xt4b, you choose
    whether the local copy goes back to draft, goes to the trash, or is left alone.
  • No inbound endpoint, no file writes. Nothing outside WordPress is contacted
    except the Xt4b API, over HTTPS.

The article arrives as rendered HTML (the API’s html field), images included:
the cover and any infographic are ordinary <img> tags on Xt4b’s image host.
WordPress renders the post title as the page’s <h1>, so the article’s own
leading <h1> is removed during import to avoid showing the title twice.

External services

This plugin makes HTTP requests to the Xt4b read API. Nothing is sent anywhere
else.

What is sent

  • The API key, as an Authorization: Bearer header.
  • The site filter from the settings, if set, as a query parameter.
  • A User-Agent header of the form Xt4b-AI-Blog-Posts/<version>; <site home URL>.

Where it is sent

To https://xt4b.com. Requests use HTTPS.

What is received

The JSON list of your own published posts (GET /api/v2/posts). Nothing is pushed
to your site.

Who operates it

Xt4b, operated by COWBOYS AND WITCHES OÜ, Tornimäe tn 5, 10145 Tallinn, Estonia.
Service terms: https://xt4b.com/terms-of-service. Privacy: https://xt4b.com/privacy.
sections.installation:
1. Copy this folder to wp-content/plugins/xt4b-ai-blog-posts.
  2. Activate Xt4b – AI Blog Posts in Plugins.
  3. Open Xt4b in the admin menu.
  4. In your Xt4b dashboard, open Settings → API, copy the key, paste it into
    the plugin, and save.
  5. Press Test connection, then Sync now.

The first sync imports every published post for the account (or for the site you
filtered to). Leave Publish as on Draft until you have looked at a few.
sections.faq:
Do I need an Xt4b account?

Yes. The plugin imports posts; Xt4b is what writes them. Without an account there
is nothing to import and the plugin does nothing at all: it fetches nothing until
you paste an API key. You can read about the product and create an account at
https://xt4b.com; the key then lives in your dashboard under Settings → API.

Where do I get an API key?

Xt4b dashboard → Settings → API. The key is read-only and can be regenerated
at any time; regenerating revokes the previous one immediately.

Does it publish automatically?

Only if you choose Publish as the import status. The schedule decides when the
plugin reads from Xt4b, not whether a post goes live.

What happens when I unpublish a post in Xt4b?

A full sync notices that the post is no longer in the published list and applies
your choice: move the local post to draft, move it to the trash, or leave it alone.
The pass is skipped when Xt4b returns zero published posts, because an empty list
is far more likely to be a misconfigured filter than a genuinely emptied account.

Will it overwrite edits I made in WordPress?

It overwrites the title, body, excerpt, slug and the Xt4b metadata when the
article’s content changes in Xt4b. A post you have not edited locally is safe; a
post you have edited will be replaced on the next content change. Set Unpublished
in Xt4b to Leave the local post alone and unpublish in Xt4b if you want to take
ownership of a post permanently.

Why is my cover image not the featured image?

Check that Featured image is enabled in the Import section of the settings.
Xt4b sends the cover as a PNG URL, so it downloads into your media library like
any other image. The one exception is a cover Xt4b could not host at publish
time: it arrives as an inline data: URI, WordPress cannot download that, and
the cover stays in post meta (_xt4b_cover_image) with the article body carrying
its own copy of the image.

Does it work with Yoast SEO or Rank Math?

Yes. When Meta tags is enabled, meta.title and meta.description are written
to the fields both plugins read.

What if I delete a post in WordPress?

It stays deleted. The importer only restores copies it trashed itself when a post
is unpublished in Xt4b (Unpublished in Xt4b → Move to trash). A post you trashed
in wp-admin is left alone, even if its content changes upstream.

Why did a sync not run on time?

WordPress runs scheduled events on page views. On a quiet site, use WP-CLI
(wp xt4b sync) from a real system cron job, or press Sync now.

What does the plugin send to Xt4b?

Two things, both to https://xt4b.com: the API key you paste in, as a bearer
token, and, because the API answers differently per site, the site filter if you
set one. The request also carries a
User-Agent identifying the plugin version and your site’s home URL. Nothing else
leaves WordPress: no post content, no user data, no telemetry. The response is
your own published posts.

1.0.0

  • First release. Imports the Xt4b v2 post shape, scheduled or on demand, with
    idempotent updates, unpublish reconciliation and WP-CLI commands.

short_description: Imports AI-written blog posts published by Xt4b into WordPress as native posts, on a schedule or on demand. Requires an Xt4b account.
